name: Derangements
whenToUse: Nobody gets their own item back: hats, letters in envelopes, a gift swap with no one drawing their own name.
example: $5$ letters are placed in $5$ addressed envelopes at random. All are wrong in $D_5 = 44$ of the $120$ ways, so the probability is $\frac{44}{120} = \frac{11}{30}$.
pitfall: Exactly $k$ items in the right place is $\binom{n}{k} D_{n-k}$, not $D_{n-k}$ alone. Memorise the small values rather than rebuilding them in the exam.
